caption: Cavalry sustained-marching shape residual (issue #959): this is the existing routing-around-terrain reproduction the issue's own investigation used -- a brittle cavalry unit breaks and flees around a hill, with a healthy enemy cavalry regiment giving chase. Before this fix, the pursuer's own formation progressively deformed during the sustained, curving chase: its Kabsch-fit shape residual (actual body positions vs the canonical slot grid, after granting the block its best-fit rotation) grew to ~50 wu RMS and its soldiers' nearest-neighbour spacing collapsed to 0.6-2 wu -- genuine body interpenetration on 20-wu mounts, not just a rigid lag. Root cause: _move_to's formed-pivot rate was paced only by the corner man's own footspeed (a purely geometric bound), with no reference to the centripetal acceleration redirecting a body's own cruising velocity actually costs -- so at a jog/sprint cruise the block could be commanded to turn sharper than its soldiers' bounded acceleration could track. The fix (UnitManeuver.max_turn_rate_for_speed, budgeted via Unit.TURN_ACCEL_BUDGET_FRACTION) caps the pivot at what the unit's own body_accel affords at its current speed, leaving half the budget free for each soldier's own arrival correction. Verified by state dump against this exact clip: the pursuer's peak shape residual drops to ~44 wu RMS and nearest-neighbour spacing stays mostly 8-20 wu through the chase instead of collapsing -- a real, substantial reduction, though the underlying dynamic (a sustained, continuously-re-aimed pivot at speed) is not fully eliminated for this pathological a case; see the PR description for the full before/after numbers and the tracked follow-up.
